Developers using GitHub Copilot have access to several AI models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. While having multiple models provides flexibility, devs often need to manually select the right model for each task. At GitHub Universe 2026, GitHub announced a new feature called GitHub Copilot Fusion, which automatically selects and combines AI models to complete coding tasks.

Screenshot of GitHub Copilot Fusion in the GitHub interface with a dark theme A dropdown menu labele

Copilot Fusion combines GitHub's existing automatic model selection technology with the multi-model orchestration capabilities of Project HydraFusion, which was introduced as a research preview in September. [...] Single: One AI model completes the task directly.
 Cascade: A cost-efficient model first attempts the task. Another model evaluates the result and decides whether a more capable model should take over.
 Critique: One model generates a response, while other models review it and provide feedback. The original model then revises its response.

The interesting part is that developers don't need to manage the above workflows. Copilot Fusion automatically decides when additional model calls are necessary, helping avoid unnecessary costs and delays for simpler tasks. [...] Instead of selecting a specific AI model, devs can now select Copilot Fusion from the model picker. Based on the complexity of the task, Copilot Fusion automatically decides which models to use and whether multiple models need to work together.

GitHub has introduced three effort levels for Copilot Fusion:

 Fusion Standard: Prioritizes efficiency and cost for everyday coding tasks.
 Fusion High: Uses more capable models and additional reasoning for complex coding tasks.
 Fusion Max: Prioritizes the most capable models for demanding tasks that require deeper reasoning.

# GitHub Launches Copilot Fusion to Automatically Select and Combine AI Models for Coding

GitHub has launched Copilot Fusion, a runtime model router and orchestrator that automatically selects AI models and execution patterns for coding tasks.

Instead of requiring developers to choose a model for each step, Fusion coordinates reasoning, code generation, debugging, and review, ultimately providing a single cohesive response.

The feature is available across all Copilot plans. It is generally available in Visual Studio Code, Copilot CLI, the GitHub Copilot app, and JetBrains IDEs. According to GitHub’s documentation, model selection remains subject to subscription entitlements and organizational policies.

## GitHub Copilot Fusion

results.content:
GitHub Copilot Fusion is GitHub’s multi-model orchestration system, made generally available on October 28, 2026, at GitHub Universe. Fusion does not answer every prompt with one model. It routes each coding task across several models and decides how they work together. GitHub built it by merging its Project HydraFusion research preview with Copilot’s automatic model selection. For developers choosing a model in Copilot’s picker, Fusion changes what that choice actually means.

## What Is GitHub Copilot Fusion

Copilot Fusion is not a single model. It is a runtime orchestration engine that picks and coordinates models for each request. GitHub Chief Product Officer Mario Rodriguez described it this way: “It’s not a model. It’s an orchestration engine at runtime.” [...] Developers select one of three effort levels instead of a specific model. Standard covers everyday coding with versatile models. High handles harder problems that need deeper reasoning. Max brings in the most capable models for complex, multi-step work. Artificial Analysis identified the model pool behind Fusion. It includes Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, and GPT-6 Sol. Which models actually run depends on the task and on organizational policy.

Fusion reflects a broader shift toward generative AI reshaping software development. That shift moves tools from single-model assistants to systems that manage multiple models on a developer’s behalf.

## How GitHub Copilot Fusion Works [...] ## How GitHub Copilot Fusion Works

Each request runs through one of three execution patterns. In Single mode, one model solves the task directly, with no handoff. Cascade starts with a cheaper, efficient model, then a quality check decides whether to escalate to a stronger one. In Critique, one model drafts an answer first. A second model reviews it, then the original model revises based on that feedback.

GitHub designed these patterns around a simple goal: automatically match task difficulty to model cost. A trivial autocomplete does not need the same model as a multi-file refactor. Fusion decides that case by case instead of leaving the choice entirely to the developer.

Developers pick the effort level. Copilot Fusion picks the models. An AT&T engineer say it's "improved token efficiency."

Source: GitHub Universe

GitHub has debuted GitHub Copilot Fusion, a new system that handles model selection and orchestration for coding tasks so developers don’t have to. [...] More compelling is the idea that developers can use Copilot Fusion to strategically switch models mid-workflow, letting the system jump between models based on what best suits each step.

After analyzing what the task requires and choosing a model, the system orchestrates the next steps based on what makes the most sense. That may be a single model doing everything, a “cascading” workflow where a quality check evaluates one model’s response and then decides to accept it or escalate it, or a “critique” workflow where one model reviews another’s work.

That could reduce the mental load for developers who may inadvertently choose inefficient models when their attention drifts.
